title: model-arch-performance-notes-llama-mistral-qwen
content:
Purpose:
This note collects ad-hoc profiling results, bottleneck hypotheses, and quick benchmarks for architecture-specific behavior: Llama-family, Mistral, Qwen, and MoE routing patterns. Intended audience: serving-runtime engineers working on kernel selection, KV-cache, routing, and compile heuristics.

Quick summary / top-level observations:
- Llama (decoder-only, dense): performs predictably with FlashAttention + fused kernels; peak throughput sensitive to sequence length distribution and KV-cache reuse.
- Mistral (sparser MLP shapes, grouped attention nuances): shows higher memory bandwidth pressure and is more sensitive to kernel tiling; quantization (8-bit) yields larger quality/runtime wins but needs custom matmul paths.
- Qwen (wide attention heads / slightly different attention projection ordering): kernel selection must prefer different GEMM layouts; we observed more thread contention in our CPU->GPU staging for medium batches.
- MoE (routing overhead): routing cost dominates at small batch sizes due to per-token top-k routing and gather/scatter overhead — throughput improves with larger batches or routing offload to fused kernels.

Hardware / testbed used:
- A100 40GB (DGX-style node), driver 525.x, CUDA 11.8.
- Also ran spot checks on H100 (driver 535.x) for flash-attention differences.
- Serving stack: runtime branch perf/llama-mistral-qwen (see PRs). Triton + custom CUDA kernels + cuBLAS as fallback.

Profiling methodology / commands used:
- Nsight Systems capture around 60s of sustained inference: nsight-sys -o capture.qdrep --trace=cuda,nvtx -- <server binary>
- CUDA-MEMCHECK & nvprof for kernel timings when Nsight inconclusive.
- Runtime-level timers: per-request latency histogram, per-token times, KV-cache hit/miss counters, dispatch time (routing), kernel-launch latency.
- Synthetic benchmarks: prompt lengths [8, 128, 1024, 4096, 8192] with batch sizes [1, 2, 8, 16] and mixed-seq length batching to simulate production.

Detailed notes by architecture:
1) Llama-2 style (7B/13B/70B)
- Observed: FlashAttention + fused qkv proj + combined MLP kernels give best performance for 13B on A100 at seq<=1024.
- Bottlenecks: For long context (>=4096), KV-cache memory and PCIe host staging become significant for 40GB cards on 32-bit offsets in some CUDA kernels (edge case where our implementation falls back to slower path).
- Mitigations tried: enable 64-bit indexing in critical kernels for >2M elements, aggressive KV-cache pinning, pre-reserving device buffers to avoid realloc overhead.
- Numbers (rough): 13B, A100, batch=1: seq=128 ~ 210 tok/s; seq=1024 ~ 85 tok/s; seq=4096 drops to ~18 tok/s without optimized KV paths. With pre-reserved KV and fused kernels seq=4096 ~ 45 tok/s.
- Open questions: test wasm-friendly kernels, verify whether enabling H100-specific kernels improves long-context BW.

2) Mistral (7B-ish family)
- Observed: Mistral variants show higher memory throughput usage; MLP block shapes (wider hidden dim) make cuBLAS matmuls less cache-friendly.
- Bottlenecks: matmul tiling and scratch allocator fragmentation; 8-bit quantization pipeline sometimes triggers suboptimal cuBLAS heuristics causing slower kernels than float16.
- Workarounds: implement custom int8 GEMM for the common shapes (w x h permutations), and use workspace-dedicated allocator to eliminate per-inference CUDA allocs.
- Numbers: Mistral-7B, A100, batch=1: seq=128 ~ 260 tok/s (float16); int8 tuned path ~ 380 tok/s but with slight perplexity regression in edge cases.
- Notes: Run more A/B quality checks on prompts in INF-2750.

3) Qwen
- Observed: Qwen variants with re-ordered q/k/v projections introduced additional kernel launches in our current graph lowering (extra transpose). Without kernel fusion we see ~10-15% overhead on small batches.
- Bottlenecks: kernel launch overhead + suboptimal transpose patterns causing poor memory coalescing.
- Mitigation: add a fused project+transpose kernel and prefer cuBLASLt with explicit layout descriptors for large GEMMs.
- Numbers: Qwen-14B-ish: batch=2 seq=256 ~ 95 tok/s baseline; with fused kernels ~115 tok/s.

4) MoE (routing-heavy models)
- Observed: at small batch sizes (1-4) routing/gating dominates CPU/GPU time. Gather/scatter for expert indices causes random memory patterns and high PCIe traffic if experts remote.
- Bottlenecks: per-token top-k selection (softmax+topk) on CPU is a major blocker; copying indices to GPU + scatter gather is expensive.
- Mitigations tested:
  - Fused GPU routing kernel (gating + topk reduced) reduces routing time by ~3x for large expert counts.
  - Batching tokens across requests to increase work per launch reduces relative routing overhead.
  - Stateless routing cache for previously seen tokens (simple LRU sketch) helps in high-reuse prompts.
- Numbers: MoE-parameterization (num_experts=64): small batch=1, seq=512 baseline ~30 tok/s; fused-routing + batch accumulation ~95 tok/s.

Long-context specific notes:
- KV-cache layout matters: interleaved vs separate buffers tradeoff between memory locality and concurrent writes. Our interleaved layout reduced kernel write amplification for dense models but increased fragmentation for MoE routed states.
- For seq > 4096 we must ensure kernels use 64-bit indexing on GPU to avoid fallback paths. Also validate allocator alignment to avoid TLB thrash.
- Prefix caching: observed large wins when requests reuse prefixes; put a lightweight prefix-hash lookup ahead of scheduling to short-circuit work.

Profiling artifacts to inspect (quick list):
- nsight captures: /artifacts/nsight/llama-13b-4096-qdrep (see linked PR above).
- perf histograms: /artifacts/perf/serving-runtime/2024-10-xx/
- kernel timelines + nvtx tags integrated into traces via runtime NVTX spans.

Immediate action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Add fused project+transpose kernel for Qwen-ish layouts (owner: Ethan) INF-2713.
- [ ] Prototype int8 GEMM for common Mistral matmul shapes and run quality evals (owner: Priya) - target benchmark sweep by EOW.
- [ ] Integrate fused GPU routing kernel into MoE path and add unit tests for correctness under top-k edge cases (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Improve allocator to pre-reserve large KV buffers and expose tuning knobs in runtime config.
- [ ] Add long-context 8k and 16k automated nightly benchmarks on H100 to catch 64-bit indexing regressions.

Notes / rough troubleshooting log (choppy):
- 2024-10-15: capture with Nsight on 13B long-context — saw big stall at copyAsync for KV slices. Pinning buffers helped.
- 2024-11-02: tried cuBLASLt heuristic override for Qwen shapes; small win but broke col-major assumption for one model variant (reverted).
- 2024-11-29: fused-routing prototype reduced MoE CPU time by ~55% in microbench. Need integration tests.

Links / references in text: Jira INF-2713 (Qwen transpose kernel), INF-2750 (Mistral int8 experiment), PRs listed above for branches and perf runs. Slack thread for MoE routing discussion.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How much of the routing overhead can be amortized by model-level re-sharding versus runtime batching? (we should run a simulation across realistic traffic traces)
- For Mistral, is the reduced latency on int8 worth the observed small perplexity regression? Need product/quality sign-off.
- Does H100 provide deterministic wins for long-context due to improved memory ops? We need a controlled H100 vs A100 run with identical kernels.

Appendix: Useful commands / snippets
- Nsight capture example:
  nsys profile --output=cap --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --kill=none -- <server> --config serving-config.yaml
- Lightweight per-token timing added via NVTX:
  NVTX_PUSH("token-start"); kernel_launch(...); NVTX_POP();
- Quick gls to artifacts: ls -lah /artifacts/nsight | tail -n 50

If anything urgent or if someone wants ownership of an action item, update this doc and ping in #eng-serving-runtime.

-- Maya
